text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The draft law on the central bank adopted by the collective presidency preserves the letter and spirit of the Dayton peace agreement, says Kasim Omicevic, a member of bank governing board. Only one institution in the country will issue money, he says.

- The new currency, "convertible mark", is worth 100 Bosnian dinars. Those who want to change Croatian kuna and Yugoslav dinars will first have to change their money into hard currency, Omicevic says.

- After Council of Ministers reached agreement on customs rates and other legislation required by the International Monetary Fund, a donors' conference for reconstruction aid may be held July, co-chairman Haris Silajdzic says.
- There are some indications that the deputy High Representative for Bosnia, Michael Steiner, could remain at his post in Sarajevo, diplomatic sources say. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
